title: Signal Lab nodes and variables
summary: Every node you can add in the Signal Lab, grouped as in the palette, and how variables work.
alternateQueries: How do I use a variable?
How do I see the waveform?

blocks.text: Right-click an empty spot on the canvas to open the palette.

blocks.definition: Sine, Saw, Square and Triangle oscillators, and Noise.
Mixer (sums inputs), Filter, Envelope, and Cross Fader (blends two inputs).
Router (selects among inputs) and Sample & Hold.
Sink (the output, in Audio or Wave (File) mode), Timeline (a node that moves a value over the length of the sound), Oscilloscope and Frequency Analyzer.
Fader Control and Button Control, driven by a MIDI control that can be learned.
Get and Set nodes for each variable you have created.

blocks.text: The Variables list on the left holds named values. Press + Variable to add one, then drag it onto the graph to place a Get node, or hold Alt while dropping to place a Set node. A variable is public (the timeline can control it) or private (only used inside the graph); public variables can be automated when the signal is used as a Signal clip.
The Compile button checks and compiles the graph. Pressing Play compiles first when the graph has changed.
A Sink in Wave (File) mode turns Play into Render: it renders straight to the project instead of starting the live engine.
